entry.title: Combined summary - BIP110 Monitor & Simulator
entry.summary: The BIP110 situation monitor tracks live miner signaling and displays the chain tips of both a core node and a BIP110 node to identify potential forks. This tool, accessible via [this link](https://bip110.orange.surf/live.html), includes visual guides on activation paths and forking dynamics, available at [activation guide](https://bip110.orange.surf/activation.html) and [forking dynamics](https://bip110.orange.surf/forking.html) respectively, as well as a simulator that explores generic soft fork chainsplit dynamics at [simulator](https://bip110.orange.surf/simulator.html). The primary goal is to provide education on these topics, particularly addressing misconceptions promoted by some proponents of this soft fork. The prediction surrounding BIP110 suggests it will not achieve the necessary 55% miner signaling within the current difficulty window, leading to mandatory signaling from block 961,632. It is expected that the initial blocks in this phase will not signal for BIP110, causing BIP110 nodes to disregard them while the standard chain continues. This scenario is anticipated to result in a miner eventually extending a stale tip, thus creating a fork with a chain that has less work. Over time, if BIP110 miners and nodes follow this lesser work chain, it could lead to a sustained fork until either capitulation occurs or a proof-of-work algorithm change is implemented. In December 2025, BIP110 was proposed under the Bitcoin Improvement Proposal framework, aiming to temporarily limit data field sizes at the consensus level to address distorted incentives arising from the support for arbitrary data. This soft fork would invalidate certain data-carrying transactions for about one year, with previously created UTXOs being exempt until the deployment expires. Once expired, all UTXOs would revert to unrestricted status. Despite its temporary nature, there's significant debate regarding the ability of consensus rules to bind future behaviors effectively. Critics argue that any continued enforcement past the expiry would be akin to a hard fork. The activation mechanism merges features from both BIP8 and BIP9, with no timeout or FAILED state, ensuring activation for enforcing nodes only if the 55% threshold of miner signaling is met before the max_activation_height. Furthermore, discussions and planning are underway within the community to monitor and collect data during the BIP-110 and BIP-300 forks slated for August 2026, as seen in ongoing conversations at [BNO Community Forum](https://bnoc.xyz/t/brainstorming-what-data-to-collect-and-monitor-during-the-bip-110-bip-300-forks-in-august-2026/139). This includes running core and BIP-110 nodes attached to fork-observer instances, with plans to live-stream the expected split when mandatory signaling begins. Concerns have been raised about the economic feasibility for miners to extend a potentially diminishing chain, questioning if external subsidies might influence such decisions.
